title: Chapter 23: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

blocks.content: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the apex regulatory authority for the securities and capital markets in India. Its primary purpose is to protect investor interests, regulate market intermediaries, and ensure orderly development of the securities market. Due to its regulatory, investigative, and quasi-judicial powers, SEBI is one of the MOST IMPORTANT regulatory bodies .
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the apex regulatory authority for the securities and capital markets in India.

items: Note that SEBI possesses three distinct powers: regulatory, investigative, and quasi-judicial.
Questions frequently test SEBI's primary mandate: protecting investor interests and regulating market intermediaries.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: SEBI is the apex regulatory authority for securities and capital markets in India.
Its main mandates are protecting investor interests, regulating market intermediaries, and fostering market development.
SEBI operates with regulatory, investigative, and quasi-judicial powers.
